nodes.text: Fall on outstretched hand (FOOSH) with anatomic snuffbox tenderness: obtain dedicated scaphoid view radiographs
**Visible scaphoid fracture with displacement (> 1 mm):** orthopaedic referral for open reduction and internal fixation
Negative initial radiographs with persistent snuffbox tenderness: place thumb spica splint or cast
**Follow-up in 10-14 days:** remove splint, re-examine, and repeat plain radiographs
**Follow-up radiographs show fracture line or callus:** continue cast immobilization for 6-12 weeks
**High-demand athlete or manual laborer:** perform early wrist MRI or CT to rule out occult fracture
Warn patient regarding risk of scaphoid nonunion and avascular necrosis due to retrograde blood supply

B.tempting: comprehensive controller for chronic pediatric asthma

algorithm.title: Pediatric asthma severity classification and management

nodes.text: Pediatric wheezing and dyspnea: classify severity by symptom frequency, nighttime awakenings, and spirometry
Intermittent asthma (symptoms <= 2 days/week, no nighttime awakenings, normal FEV1): prescribe SABA PRN only
**Mild persistent asthma (symptoms > 2 days/week, nighttime awakenings 3-4/month):** add daily low-dose inhaled corticosteroid
**Moderate persistent asthma (daily symptoms, nighttime awakenings > 1/week):** prescribe daily low-dose ICS-LABA or medium-dose ICS
**Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction:** administer SABA or low-dose ICS-formoterol 5-15 minutes before exercise
Manage comorbid allergic rhinitis with daily intranasal fluticasone and environmental allergen avoidance
Provide written asthma action plan and re-evaluate control every 3 to 6 months

acute-otitis-media.name: Acute otitis media
acute-otitis-media.scope: Bulging erythematous tympanic membrane, impaired mobility, oral amoxicillin first-line, amoxicillin-clavulanate, tympanostomy indications
acute-otitis-media.core: Acute otalgia with middle-ear effusion and a bulging tympanic membrane identifies acute otitis media; age, laterality, and severity guide antibiotics.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Young age, daycare, viral URI, tobacco smoke exposure, absent breastfeeding
Craniofacial abnormalities and eustachian tube dysfunction increase recurrence

rows.label: Clues
items: Ear tugging, fever, irritability, poor feeding; spontaneous perforation causes new otorrhea
★ **Postauricular swelling/tenderness, protruding pinna** → mastoiditis
Erythematous membrane alone, especially during crying, insufficient for diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: URI-related eustachian edema traps fluid; pneumococcus, nontypeable H influenzae, Moraxella commonly infect middle ear

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pneumatic otoscopy**: reduced mobility supports effusion; moderate/severe bulging or nonexternal otorrhea diagnostic
Mild bulging requires recent otalgia or intense erythema; no effusion → no AOM diagnosis
Tympanometry if effusion uncertain; routine imaging and cultures unnecessary
Failure after 48–72 h → repeat examination; persistent effusion alone does not mean antibiotic failure

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Acetaminophen or ibuprofen** for pain regardless of antibiotic decision
★ When treating → **amoxicillin 80–90 mg/kg/day**; 10 days if <2 years or severe
Recent amoxicillin within 30 days, purulent conjunctivitis, or amoxicillin failure → amoxicillin-clavulanate
Selected older nonsevere cases → 5–7 days; severe illness/complication or oral intolerance changes regimen
★ Recurrent AOM **≥3/6 months or ≥4/12 months** → tube evaluation; effusion required at candidacy assessment

rows.label: Complications
items: Conductive hearing loss, membrane perforation, mastoiditis, rare intracranial infection
Effusion ≥3 months → hearing assessment; tubes considered for bilateral persistent fluid with hearing difficulty

rows.label: Prevention
items: Pneumococcal/influenza vaccination, breastfeeding, smoke avoidance; no routine prophylactic antibiotics
Observe speech/hearing development in recurrent disease

rows.label: Mimics
items: Otitis media with effusion: fluid without acute inflammatory illness
Otitis externa: canal inflammation, pain with tragus/pinna movement
Referred dental/TMJ pain: normal middle-ear examination

acute-rheumatic-fever.name: Acute rheumatic fever
acute-rheumatic-fever.scope: Post-streptococcal sequela, revised Jones criteria (carditis, migratory polyarthritis, chorea), ASO titers, penicillin and prophylaxis
acute-rheumatic-fever.core: Immune-mediated illness weeks after group A streptococcal infection, featuring migratory arthritis, carditis, or chorea; prevent recurrent valve injury with antibiotic prophylaxis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: School-aged children, crowding, limited access to care, prior rheumatic fever; higher-risk endemic populations

rows.label: Clues
items: Migratory large-joint inflammation, new mitral regurgitation murmur, tachycardia out of proportion to fever
★ **Sydenham chorea**: involuntary movements, emotional lability, milkmaid grip; may appear months later
Erythema marginatum: evanescent nonpruritic rings; painless subcutaneous nodules over extensor surfaces

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Molecular mimicry between streptococcal antigens and host tissues → inflammatory injury; not direct cardiac infection

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Initial episode: **2 major or 1 major + 2 minor**, plus preceding GAS evidence
ASO/anti-DNase B rise or positive throat testing supports prior infection; titers do not prove active infection
★ **Doppler echocardiography for all suspected cases**; subclinical valvulitis counts as carditis
Isolated chorea or indolent carditis can establish diagnosis despite absent contemporaneous GAS evidence
High-risk populations use broader joint criteria and lower inflammatory cutoffs; avoid counting one feature twice

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Penicillin eradication** even if throat culture negative; naproxen or aspirin for arthritis
Carditis with heart failure → diuresis and cardiology care; severe chorea → valproate or carbamazepine
Severe carditis may receive glucocorticoids; anti-inflammatory drugs do not replace recurrence prophylaxis

rows.label: Complications
items: Chronic rheumatic valve disease: mitral stenosis/regurgitation, atrial fibrillation, embolism, heart failure
Recurrent attacks accelerate permanent valvular damage

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat GAS pharyngitis promptly; secondary benzathine penicillin usually every 4 weeks
No carditis: ≥5 years and through age 21; resolved carditis: ≥10 years and through 21
Residual valve disease: continue ≥10 years and through age 40; selected patients lifelong

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic arthritis: one persistently inflamed joint, positive aspirate
Poststreptococcal reactive arthritis: less migratory, poorer NSAID response
Endocarditis: bacteremia, vegetations, persistent systemic infection

acute-rhinosinusitis.name: Acute rhinosinusitis
acute-rhinosinusitis.scope: Common cold, viral rhinosinusitis, acute bacterial rhinosinusitis criteria, symptomatic therapy, antibiotic stewardship
acute-rhinosinusitis.core: Acute nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, and facial pressure usually reflect a self-limited viral infection; duration and course identify likely bacterial disease.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Respiratory exposure, daycare contacts, impaired drainage from allergic inflammation
Immunocompromise, recent antibiotics, or hospitalization increases resistant-organism risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Cough, reduced smell, maxillary tenderness; colored mucus alone does not establish bacterial infection
★ Orbital swelling, painful eye movement, reduced vision, severe headache → **complicated infection**

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Viral mucosal edema blocks sinus drainage; secondary infection commonly pneumococcus, H influenzae, or Moraxella

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Clinical diagnosis**; uncomplicated illness needs neither sinus radiographs nor CT
Persistent, severe, or biphasic course identifies bacterial cases; fever alone is insufficient
Suspected orbital/intracranial extension → contrast CT; MRI for intracranial definition
Refractory or unusual infection → ENT evaluation; routine nasal swab cultures unhelpful

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Viral illness → **saline irrigation, acetaminophen/NSAID**; no antibiotics
Intranasal fluticasone for associated allergic inflammation; topical oxymetazoline at most 3 days
★ Uncomplicated bacterial illness + reliable follow-up → **watchful waiting** or antibiotics
Antibiotic choice: amoxicillin-clavulanate, usually 5–7 days in adults; penicillin allergy → doxycycline
Complication → admission, IV ampicillin-sulbactam, urgent ENT/ophthalmology; avoid empiric azithromycin because resistance

rows.label: Complications
items: Orbital cellulitis or abscess, cavernous sinus thrombosis, meningitis, intracranial abscess
Unnecessary antibiotics → diarrhea, C difficile, resistance

rows.label: Prevention
items: Hand hygiene, smoking avoidance, control allergic rhinitis
Sterile/distilled or previously boiled water for nasal irrigation

rows.label: Mimics
items: Allergic rhinitis: itching, sneezing, watery discharge without fever
Migraine: episodic disabling headache, photophobia, nausea
Dental infection: focal tooth pain, unilateral maxillary symptoms

table.title: Bacterial patterns
rows: Initial improvement → new fever or worsening symptoms

adult-immunizations.name: Adult immunizations
adult-immunizations.scope: Routine adult vaccines, immunocompromised and HIV, pregnancy, live-vaccine contraindications, chronic medical conditions (COPD, diabetes, liver disease), vaccine counseling and addressing hesitancy
adult-immunizations.core: Match vaccination to age, prior doses, pregnancy, immune status, and exposure risk; missed series resume without restarting.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ **HepB**: all adults 19–59; ≥60 with risk or requesting protection
Liver disease → HepA/HepB; COPD, diabetes, smoking → pneumococcal before routine age
Asplenia → pneumococcal, MenACWY, MenB, Hib; HIV → MenACWY

rows.label: Start/stop
items: ★ Pregnancy: **Tdap each pregnancy at 27–36 wk**; inactivated influenza any trimester
Maternal RSV: Abrysvo at 32–36 wk, September–January; previous pregnancy dose → infant antibody instead
RSV once: all ≥75; ages 50–74 with increased severe-disease risk

rows.label: Test
items: Review records, contraindications, immunity; HBV serology useful, but **do not delay vaccination**
★ Immunocompromised ≥19 → recombinant zoster; HIV CD4 ≥200 permits MMR/varicella if nonimmune
HPV started <15 → two doses; ≥15 or immunocompromised → three

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Avoid live MMR, varicella, intranasal influenza** during pregnancy or severe immunosuppression
PCV15 → PPSV23: minimum 8 weeks if immunocompromised; mild illness/antibiotics need no deferral
Hesitancy → elicit concern, explain benefit, recommend clearly; refusal → document, revisit

table.title: Routine adult schedule
rows: Annual influenza; updated COVID-19 for all adults
Tdap once, then either every 10 years
PCV20/21 alone; PCV15 → PPSV23 after 1 year

alcohol-use-disorder.name: Alcohol use disorder
alcohol-use-disorder.scope: Unhealthy alcohol use, CAGE and AUDIT screening, transaminitis (AST > ALT), motivational interviewing, naltrexone, acamprosate
alcohol-use-disorder.core: Compulsive alcohol use despite harm, impaired control, or physiologic dependence calls for nonjudgmental assessment and relapse-prevention treatment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Family history, early initiation, trauma, depression, anxiety, social stress
Binge drinking and escalating tolerance; coexisting sedative use increases overdose risk

rows.label: Clues
items: Craving, failed attempts to cut down, role impairment, continued use despite consequences
AST:ALT >2, macrocytosis, elevated GGT support exposure but neither prove nor exclude disorder
★ Tremor, tachycardia, hallucinations, seizures after reduction → **withdrawal**, potentially fatal

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Chronic GABA enhancement/NMDA inhibition → compensatory adaptation; cessation unmasks CNS excitation
Mesolimbic reinforcement and stress circuitry sustain compulsive use and relapse

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Screen adults using **AUDIT-C** or single-question heavy-use screen; positive result → fuller assessment
DSM-5: ≥2 of 11 criteria within 12 months; 2–3 mild, 4–5 moderate, ≥6 severe
CAGE: Cut down, Annoyed, Guilty, Eye-opener; ≥2 positive suggests problem use, misses early risky drinking
Assess suicidality, other drugs, liver disease, nutritional deficiency, pregnancy, withdrawal history

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Motivational interviewing**: elicit goals, reflect ambivalence, agree achievable change; CBT and mutual support
Withdrawal → benzodiazepines; inpatient detoxification for severe history, unstable comorbidity, or unreliable support
Thiamine promptly for malnutrition/Wernicke risk; never delay emergency glucose for hypoglycemia
Disulfiram: selected supervised abstinence; avoid severe liver/cardiac disease; alcohol exposure causes aversive reaction

rows.label: Complications
items: Cirrhosis, pancreatitis, cardiomyopathy, neuropathy, cancer, injuries, fetal alcohol effects
Wernicke encephalopathy → Korsakoff amnesia; depression and suicide risk

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Ongoing **relapse planning**, frequent follow-up, social support; abstinence for pregnancy or advanced liver disease
Assess hepatitis vaccination, nutrition, driving safety, medication interactions

rows.label: Mimics
items: Sedative withdrawal: similar autonomic excitation with benzodiazepine/barbiturate reduction
Hyperthyroidism: tremor/tachycardia without alcohol-linked time course

table.title: Relapse prevention
rows: Current opioids; acute hepatitis/severe hepatic failure

alcohol-use-disorder.evidence: Not checked online; established screening and addiction-treatment principles.

asthma.name: Asthma
asthma.scope: Diagnosis, stepwise therapy, acute exacerbation, exercise-induced bronchoconstriction
asthma.core: Variable episodes of wheeze, cough, dyspnea, and chest tightness from reversible expiratory airflow limitation.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Atopy, family history, allergens, viral infections, smoke, occupational sensitizers
Exercise/cold air, aspirin-sensitive disease, nonselective beta-blockers; assess workplace symptom pattern

rows.label: Clues
items: Nocturnal/early-morning symptoms; normal examination between attacks
★ **Silent chest, exhaustion, altered mentation, rising PaCO2** → impending respiratory failure
Acute attack: low peak flow, accessory-muscle use, difficulty speaking

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Airway inflammation, smooth-muscle constriction, mucus → variable obstruction and hyperresponsiveness
Persistent uncontrolled inflammation → remodeling with incompletely reversible airflow limitation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Spirometry**: obstruction with bronchodilator FEV1 increase >12% and >200 mL in adults
Normal spirometry with suspicion → repeat during symptoms or methacholine challenge
Exercise challenge: postexercise FEV1 fall >10%; assess baseline control before isolated exercise diagnosis

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Exacerbation → **repeated inhaled albuterol + ipratropium**, oxygen, early systemic glucocorticoids
Severe poor response → IV magnesium; deterioration → intubation; avoid sedatives and routine antibiotics
Exercise symptoms → preexercise albuterol or prescribed ICS-formoterol; persistent symptoms → improve controller
Check technique/adherence before stepping up; uncontrolled despite high-dose ICS-LABA → phenotype-directed biologic referral

rows.label: Complications
items: Status asthmaticus, pneumothorax, respiratory arrest
ICS → thrush/dysphonia; systemic steroids → osteoporosis, hyperglycemia, adrenal suppression

rows.label: Prevention
items: Written action plan, trigger reduction, smoking cessation, spacer; rinse mouth after ICS
★ **No SABA-only treatment or LABA monotherapy**; current GINA differs from older intermittent-asthma teaching

rows.label: Mimics
items: Inducible laryngeal obstruction: inspiratory stridor, inspiratory flow-loop flattening
COPD: persistent obstruction, smoking history
HF: edema, elevated JVP, cardiac findings

attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder.name: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder
attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder.scope: Diagnostic criteria across two settings, behavioral rating scales from parents and teachers, behavioral therapy, stimulant pharmacotherapy
attention-deficit-hyperactivity-disorder.core: Persistent developmentally inappropriate inattention and/or hyperactivity–impulsivity causing functional impairment across settings, with childhood onset.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Strong genetic contribution, prematurity, prenatal tobacco/alcohol exposure; symptoms may persist into adulthood
Learning disorders, anxiety, oppositional behavior, sleep problems and substance use commonly coexist

rows.label: Clues
items: Inattention: lost items, distraction, disorganization; hyperactivity: fidgeting, leaving seat, excessive talking
Impulsivity: interrupting, difficulty waiting; presentations can be inattentive, hyperactive–impulsive, or combined
Academic difficulty alone insufficient; assess family, peer, driving, and workplace function

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Altered dopamine/norepinephrine executive-control signaling; inconsistent performance does not imply deliberate behavior

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **≥6 symptoms per domain**, or ≥5 if age ≥17; duration ≥6 months
★ Several symptoms **before age 12**, present in ≥2 settings, with impairment; exclude better explanations
Parent and teacher DSM-based rating scales, such as Vanderbilt; interview child and evaluate comorbidities
Check vision/hearing, sleep, learning needs; no routine EEG, neuroimaging, or laboratory diagnostic test

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Ages 4–5: **parent-training behavioral management** first; methylphenidate for persistent moderate/severe impairment
★ Age ≥6: **methylphenidate or amphetamine** plus behavioral/classroom intervention and educational supports
Atomoxetine, extended-release guanfacine/clonidine when stimulants unsuitable, ineffective, or diversion concerning
Before prescribing: personal/family cardiac history, BP/HR, height/weight; ECG only if cardiac concern
Titrate to function and adverse effects; monitor appetite, sleep, growth, BP, misuse; reassess across settings

rows.label: Complications
items: Injury, academic failure, relationship problems; untreated impairment increases later substance-use risk
Stimulants → appetite suppression, insomnia, tachycardia; atomoxetine → suicidality warning, rare liver injury

rows.label: Prevention
items: Routines, sleep, positive reinforcement, school accommodations; secure medication against diversion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Absence seizures: brief stereotyped unresponsiveness with abrupt recovery
Anxiety: attention disrupted by worry
Sleep apnea: snoring, poor sleep, daytime behavioral dysfunction

benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.name: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.scope: Lower urinary tract symptoms, medical therapy, urinary retention and obstructive uropathy
benign-prostatic-hyperplasia.core: Aging man with hesitancy, weak stream, incomplete emptying, and nocturia from benign periurethral prostatic enlargement.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Increasing age, androgen exposure, family history, obesity/metabolic syndrome
Anticholinergics, opioids, and sympathomimetic decongestants can precipitate retention

rows.label: Clues
items: Storage symptoms: urgency, frequency; voiding symptoms: straining, intermittency, terminal dribbling
Smooth, symmetric enlarged prostate; size correlates imperfectly with symptom severity
★ **Painful inability to void** with palpable bladder → acute urinary retention
Renal dysfunction or bilateral hydronephrosis suggests high-pressure obstruction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Dihydrotestosterone-driven transition-zone hyperplasia + alpha-adrenergic smooth-muscle tone obstruct bladder outlet

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Urinalysis**, symptom score, examination; review medications and neurologic disease
Postvoid residual if incomplete emptying suspected; creatinine/renal ultrasound for obstruction or renal impairment
PSA after shared decision-making if result changes management; elevation not specific for cancer

rows.label: Tx
items: Mild, nonbothersome → observation; reduce evening fluids, caffeine, alcohol; timed voiding
★ Acute retention → **urethral catheter**, then alpha-blocker and voiding trial; suprapubic drainage if catheterization fails
★ Refractory symptoms, retention, recurrent UTIs, stones, renal impairment → **TURP or other outlet procedure**
Monitor urine output/electrolytes after relief of prolonged obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Overflow incontinence, recurrent infection, bladder stones, postrenal AKI
Postobstructive diuresis; surgery → bleeding, retrograde ejaculation, urethral stricture

rows.label: Prevention
items: Avoid precipitating drugs; reassess progressive symptoms and residual volume
BPH does not transform into prostate cancer; continue independent cancer-risk discussion

rows.label: Mimics
items: Prostate cancer: hard asymmetric nodule
Prostatitis: tender prostate, fever; neurogenic bladder: neurologic disease, altered bladder sensation

table.title: Medication selection
rows: Large gland; reduce progression over months

celiac-disease.name: Celiac disease
celiac-disease.scope: Gluten-sensitive enteropathy, malabsorption, iron deficiency anemia, dermatitis herpetiformis, IgA anti-tTG, small bowel villous atrophy, gluten-free diet
celiac-disease.core: Gluten-triggered autoimmune small-bowel injury causing malabsorption or unexplained iron deficiency, sometimes with intensely pruritic extensor-surface dermatitis herpetiformis.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: First-degree relative, type 1 diabetes, autoimmune thyroid disease, selective IgA deficiency
HLA-DQ2/DQ8 susceptibility; positive genotype common and not diagnostic

rows.label: Clues
items: Chronic diarrhea, steatorrhea, bloating, weight loss; constipation or minimal GI symptoms possible
Iron deficiency refractory to oral replacement, aphthous ulcers, low bone density
Children: poor growth/delayed puberty; severe disease: hypoalbuminemia, edema, vitamin deficiencies

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Tissue transglutaminase modifies gliadin → T-cell response damages proximal intestinal mucosa
Impaired absorption → iron/folate/calcium deficiency; cutaneous granular IgA deposition causes rash

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ While **eating gluten → IgA anti-tTG + total IgA**; gluten restriction causes false negatives
★ IgA deficiency → **IgG anti-tTG or deamidated gliadin peptide antibodies**
★ Adults: positive serology or high suspicion → **EGD with multiple duodenal biopsies**, even if mucosa normal
Biopsy: villous atrophy, crypt hyperplasia, intraepithelial lymphocytes; high suspicion overrides negative serology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ **Lifelong gluten-free diet**: avoid wheat, barley, rye; dietitian, cross-contamination counseling
Pure uncontaminated oats usually tolerated; replace iron, folate, calcium, vitamin D and other measured deficiencies
Dermatitis herpetiformis: dapsone for rapid relief after G6PD testing; diet treats underlying intestinal injury
Persistent symptoms → assess gluten exposure, alternative diagnoses; refractory disease → specialist before immunosuppression

rows.label: Complications
items: Osteoporosis, infertility; untreated disease → enteropathy-associated T-cell lymphoma, small-bowel adenocarcinoma
Dapsone → hemolysis/methemoglobinemia; restrictive diet → nutritional imbalance

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Follow **symptoms, nutritional labs, anti-tTG trend**; persistent elevation suggests gluten exposure
Bone-density assessment in adults with risk/malabsorption; test symptomatic first-degree relatives
No proven primary prevention; do not start gluten exclusion before diagnostic testing

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS: no objective malabsorption, anemia, or inflammatory injury
Giardiasis: contaminated water exposure, stool antigen/PCR positive
Pancreatic insufficiency: low fecal elastase, pancreatic risk history

child-growth-and-development.name: Child growth and development
child-growth-and-development.scope: Normal growth velocity, weight doubling and tripling milestones, WHO/CDC growth chart interpretation, developmental surveillance, normal toddler behavioral variants (head banging, temper tantrums)
child-growth-and-development.core: Interpret serial growth and developmental progress against age, family pattern, and corrected gestational age; a trajectory matters more than one percentile.

rows.label: Definition
items: Weight doubles by 4–6 months, triples by 12 months, quadruples near 24 months
Length increases about 25 cm during year 1; prepubertal height velocity about 5–6 cm/year
★ **WHO charts before 2 years; CDC charts from 2 years** in US practice

rows.label: Interpret
items: Nutrition failure: weight falls first; endocrine disease: height slows with preserved/increased weight
★ Downward crossing **2 major percentile channels** → assess intake, disease, measurement error
Correct prematurity through about 2 years; track infant head circumference

rows.label: Use when
items: Developmental surveillance every visit; standardized general screens at 9, 18, and 30 months
★ **Regression/missed milestones → early intervention**, hearing/vision assessment, targeted evaluation
BMI-for-age from 2 years; weight-for-length younger; consider parental heights and pubertal timing

rows.label: Compare
items: Toddler tantrums → routines, calm limits, positive reinforcement; avoid rewarding demands
Head banging at sleep onset often self-soothing; assess injuries and daytime development

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **One percentile cannot diagnose disease**; stable proportional smallness may be familial
Persistent skill loss needs evaluation; never wait for school failure

child-growth-and-development.evidence: Checked screening ages 2026-10-30: [AAP surveillance/screening](https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/developmental-surveillance-and-screening-patient-care/); growth facts established pediatric teaching.

childhood-and-adolescent-immunizations.name: Childhood and adolescent immunizations
childhood-and-adolescent-immunizations.scope: Routine pediatric vaccine schedule, adolescent immunizations (meningococcal conjugate, HPV, Tdap), catch-up vaccination guidelines
childhood-and-adolescent-immunizations.core: Vaccinate before exposure; use age, prior doses, minimum intervals, and immune status to choose the next dose.

rows.label: Who
items: All children; AAP 2026 schedule retains broad routine childhood protection

rows.label: Schedule
items: ★ 11–12 years: **Tdap, MenACWY**; MenACWY booster at 16 years
AAP HPV: start 9–12 years; <15 years → two doses, 6–12 months apart
HPV initiation ≥15 years or immunocompromised → three doses at 0, 1–2, 6 months

rows.label: Special groups
items: ★ Catch-up: **never restart**; respect minimum ages and intervals
Asplenia/complement defects: extra meningococcal/pneumococcal doses; annual influenza from 6 months
HBsAg-positive mother: HepB vaccine + HBIG within 12 hours of birth

rows.label: Choice
items: MenB: shared decision, usually 16–23 years; high-risk patients need earlier protection

rows.label: Contraindications
items: ★ Live vaccines: pregnancy, severe immunodeficiency; prior anaphylaxis precludes that vaccine
Rotavirus: SCID or prior intussusception; first dose by 14 weeks 6 days

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **AAP/classic boards: multidose HPV**; federal 2026 policy: one dose
Mild illness, antibiotics, breastfeeding → vaccination proceeds; rotavirus series ends by 8 months
Separate injectable live vaccines ≥4 weeks unless simultaneous; IVIG can delay MMR/varicella

table.title: Routine AAP childhood schedule
rows: First vaccination <9 years: two ≥4 weeks apart

constipation-and-fecal-impaction.name: Constipation and fecal impaction
constipation-and-fecal-impaction.scope: Functional constipation, medication-induced constipation, fecal impaction and overflow incontinence, digital disimpaction, laxatives, fiber
constipation-and-fecal-impaction.core: Difficult, infrequent, or incomplete defecation; loose stool can represent overflow around an impacted rectal stool mass.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Low fiber, immobility, dehydration, withholding, older age; childhood onset often follows painful defecation/toilet training
Opioids, anticholinergics, iron, calcium, verapamil; hypothyroidism, hypercalcemia, neurologic disease

rows.label: Clues
items: Hard/lumpy stool, straining, incomplete emptying, <3 spontaneous stools/week; frequency alone insufficient
★ **Rectal fullness, paradoxical diarrhea, fecal soiling, urinary retention** → consider impaction
★ **Bleeding, anemia, weight loss, new persistent change**, severe distension/vomiting → structural evaluation

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Slow transit increases water absorption; pelvic-floor dyssynergia prevents coordinated expulsion
Stool retention stretches rectum → reduced sensation and leakage of liquid around retained mass

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ History, drug review, abdominal examination, **digital rectal examination** for stool, masses, pelvic-floor dysfunction
No alarm findings → clinical diagnosis; targeted TSH/calcium if suspected; colonoscopy for alarms or overdue screening
Refractory despite laxatives → anorectal manometry + balloon-expulsion test; then transit studies if needed
Empty rectum does not exclude proximal impaction; obstruction concern → abdominal imaging

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Palpable hard rectal mass → **manual disimpaction**, then enemas; proximal stool → PEG after obstruction excluded
★ Uncomplicated constipation → **fiber gradually + polyethylene glycol**; hydration if depleted, scheduled postmeal toileting
Dyssynergic defecation → pelvic-floor biofeedback; stool softener alone will not correct outlet dysfunction
Opioid-induced: stimulant + osmotic laxative; refractory → naloxegol/naldemedine after excluding bowel obstruction

rows.label: Complications
items: Anal fissures, hemorrhoids, prolapse, stercoral ulceration/perforation, recurrent impaction
Magnesium laxatives → hypermagnesemia in CKD; phosphate enemas → electrolyte injury, especially renal disease

rows.label: Prevention
items: Maintenance bowel regimen after disimpaction; regular activity, adequate dietary fiber, minimize constipating drugs
Avoid bulk fiber during unresolved impaction; pediatric withholding → reward-based routine, no punishment

rows.label: Mimics
items: IBS-C: recurrent abdominal pain related to defecation/stool changes
Bowel obstruction: colicky pain, vomiting, obstipation, dilated bowel
Hirschsprung: neonatal delayed meconium, distension, absent rectoanal inhibitory reflex

table.title: Escalating agents
rows: Limited efficacy; avoid relying on it

constipation-and-fecal-impaction.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [AGA/ACG constipation guideline 2023](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10544839/); impaction and diagnostic pathways established teaching.

depressive-disorders.name: Depressive disorders
depressive-disorders.scope: Major depressive disorder criteria, depression in older adults, bereavement vs MDD, pharmacotherapy, psychotherapy, suicide risk
depressive-disorders.core: Persistent low mood or loss of pleasure with neurovegetative and cognitive symptoms, causing clinically significant distress or impaired function.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior episodes, family history, chronic illness/pain, substance use, postpartum period, social isolation
Older adults: disability, bereavement, polypharmacy; depression may present as somatic complaints

rows.label: Clues
items: SIGECAPS: sleep, interest, guilt, energy, concentration, appetite, psychomotor change, suicidality
Psychotic depression: delusions/hallucinations only during mood episodes, often guilt or nihilism
★ **Suicide risk**: prior attempt, intent, plan, means, agitation, psychosis, intoxication

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Multifactorial mood-circuit dysfunction involving monoamines, stress responses, and neuroplasticity
Antidepressant benefit develops over weeks despite early changes in neurotransmitter availability

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ MDD: **≥5 symptoms for ≥2 weeks**, including depressed mood or anhedonia; exclude mania/hypomania
PHQ-9 quantifies severity; interview establishes diagnosis; assess substances, drugs, TSH/CBC when clinically suspected
★ **Ask directly about suicide**, access to firearms, protective factors; questioning does not increase risk

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Imminent danger → **continuous observation and psychiatric hospitalization**; remove lethal means
Mild: CBT/interpersonal psychotherapy; moderate/severe: SSRI such as sertraline + psychotherapy
★ Urgent suicidality/catatonia/anorexia → **ECT**; psychotic depression → ECT or antidepressant + antipsychotic
Continue antidepressant ≥6 months after remission; recurrent/severe episodes → longer maintenance

rows.label: Complications
items: Suicide, malnutrition, functional decline, recurrence
SSRIs: sexual dysfunction, GI effects, hyponatremia; early activation/suicidality monitoring, especially age <25
Bupropion: seizures; avoid eating disorders; mirtazapine: weight gain/sedation, useful with anorexia/insomnia

rows.label: Prevention
items: Safety plan, early follow-up after starting/changing drugs, family support with consent
Taper antidepressants to reduce discontinuation symptoms; avoid antidepressant monotherapy in bipolar disorder

rows.label: Mimics
items: Dementia: insidious consistent deficits; depressive cognitive impairment often prominent complaints and variable effort
Hypothyroidism: cold intolerance, constipation, elevated TSH

table.title: Distinguishing persistent sadness
rows: Waves tied to reminders; self-esteem usually preserved
Pervasive worthlessness; bereavement does not exclude diagnosis
Stressor within 3 months; MDD criteria absent

ectopic-pregnancy.name: Ectopic pregnancy
ectopic-pregnancy.scope: Diagnosis (beta-hCG, transvaginal ultrasound, discriminatory zone), unruptured ectopic pregnancy, medical management (methotrexate), ruptured ectopic pregnancy, surgical management
ectopic-pregnancy.core: Pregnancy implanted outside the endometrial cavity, usually tubal; early pregnancy with pelvic pain or bleeding requires localization and rupture assessment.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prior ectopic, PID/tubal damage, tubal surgery, infertility treatment, smoking
IUDs prevent pregnancy overall; pregnancy despite IUD has higher ectopic proportion; many cases lack risks

rows.label: Clues
items: Amenorrhea, unilateral pelvic pain, spotting; cervical motion/adnexal tenderness nonspecific
★ **Syncope, shoulder-tip pain, peritoneal signs, hypotension** → hemoperitoneum/rupture
Heterotopic pregnancy possible despite visualized intrauterine pregnancy, particularly after assisted reproduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Impaired tubal transport → extrauterine trophoblastic implantation, invasion, hemorrhage
Methotrexate inhibits folate-dependent DNA synthesis in proliferating trophoblast

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Pregnancy test → quantitative beta-hCG + transvaginal ultrasound**; ultrasound regardless of hCG when symptomatic
Extrauterine yolk sac/embryo diagnostic; adnexal mass/free fluid supportive; empty uterus alone insufficient
★ Stable pregnancy of unknown location → **repeat hCG in 48 hours**, serial ultrasound until resolved/localized
Discriminatory threshold up to 3,500 mIU/mL protects viable IUP; abnormal rise/fall cannot establish location

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Unstable/rupture concern → **IV access, blood resuscitation, urgent surgery**; do not await serial hCG
Confirmed unruptured, stable, reliable follow-up, low hCG, no fetal heartbeat → consider **methotrexate**
Avoid methotrexate: viable IUP, breastfeeding, hepatic/renal disease, cytopenias, immunodeficiency, unreliable follow-up
Postmethotrexate hCG days 4/7: fall ≥15% → weekly until negative; inadequate fall → reassess/re-dose/surgery

rows.label: Complications
items: Hemorrhagic shock, death, tubal loss, recurrence, impaired fertility
Methotrexate: mucositis, hepatotoxicity, marrow suppression; rupture remains possible despite falling hCG

rows.label: Prevention
items: Treat/prevent STIs, smoking cessation; prior ectopic → early ultrasound in subsequent pregnancy
Methotrexate counseling: avoid alcohol, folate supplements, intercourse until resolution; avoid conception for 3 months
Unsensitized Rh-negative ectopic → Rh(D) immune globulin; provide return precautions for escalating pain/dizziness

rows.label: Mimics
items: Miscarriage: intrauterine pregnancy loss; passage of decidual tissue alone does not prove IUP
Hemorrhagic corpus luteum: ovarian source, may coexist with normal pregnancy
Ovarian torsion: abrupt severe unilateral pain, enlarged ovary

table.title: Alternative definitive branches
rows: Stable, minimal symptoms, low declining hCG
Selected expectant management with reliable surveillance
Heartbeat, high hCG, or medical contraindication

ectopic-pregnancy.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACOG ectopic pregnancy](https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/ectopic-pregnancy), [NICE tubal ectopic management](https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/NG126/chapter/management-of-tubal-ectopic-pregnancy); conservative discriminatory threshold established ACOG teaching.

elbow-injuries.name: Elbow injuries
elbow-injuries.scope: Supracondylar fracture of the humerus, radial head subluxation, elbow dislocation, fat pad signs, lateral and medial epicondylitis, counterforce bracing, cubital tunnel syndrome
elbow-injuries.core: Age, mechanism, deformity, and precise tenderness separate elbow fracture/dislocation from traction injury, tendinopathy, and nerve compression.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Fall onto outstretched hand → fracture/dislocation; longitudinal forearm pull → pediatric radial-head subluxation
Repetitive wrist loading → epicondylitis; prolonged elbow flexion/pressure → ulnar nerve compression

rows.label: Clues
items: Pain, swelling, limited motion after trauma; open wound or tense swelling increases urgency
★ **Absent pulse, cool hand, worsening pain with passive stretch** → vascular injury/compartment syndrome
Check median/anterior interosseous, radial, ulnar function before and after reduction

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Pediatric annular-ligament displacement restricts rotation; displaced distal humerus can injure brachial artery
Overuse tendon degeneration differs from inflammatory arthritis; cubital tunnel compresses the ulnar nerve

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ Trauma/deformity → **AP/lateral radiographs**; posterior fat pad indicates occult intra-articular fracture
Anterior humeral line missing capitellum supports displaced supracondylar fracture
Classic nursemaid presentation without swelling/bony tenderness → clinical diagnosis; image atypical or failed reduction
Nerve-conduction testing for uncertain or persistent cubital neuropathy

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Supracondylar fracture: **splint and urgent orthopedics**; displaced/vascularly compromised → reduction and pinning
Elbow dislocation → reduction, repeat neurovascular examination/films, early supervised motion
★ Nursemaid elbow → **hyperpronation** or supination-flexion; reassess spontaneous arm use
Tendinopathy: rest, NSAIDs, rehabilitation, counterforce brace; cubital tunnel: avoid flexion/pressure, night splint

rows.label: Complications
items: Volkmann ischemic contracture, malunion/cubitus varus, persistent neuropathy
Dislocation → stiffness, instability, heterotopic ossification; immobilization worsens loss of motion

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Lift children **under the arms**, avoiding traction on hands/wrists
Ergonomic tools, gradual load progression, stretching/strengthening; pad elbow during repetitive contact

rows.label: Mimics
items: Septic joint: fever, effusion, severe passive-motion pain
Radial-head fracture: adult fall, lateral tenderness, painful pronation/supination

table.title: Overuse localization
rows: Medial pain during wrist flexion/pronation against resistance

elbow-injuries.evidence: Not checked online; established orthopedic and peripheral nerve principles.

elder-abuse-and-neglect.name: Elder abuse and neglect
elder-abuse-and-neglect.scope: Physical abuse, psychological abuse, neglect, financial exploitation, clinical red flags, reporting to adult protective services
elder-abuse-and-neglect.core: Unexplained injury, unmet basic needs, intimidation, or loss of financial control warrants private assessment, safety planning, and mandated reporting.

rows.label: Principle
items: Respect autonomy while protecting vulnerable adults; decision-making capacity is specific to the decision
Dependence, cognitive impairment, isolation, caregiver strain, and coercion increase vulnerability

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Interview separately**; ask about safety, threats, caregiving, finances, basic needs
★ Stabilize injuries; assess cognition, capacity, suicidality, immediate danger, and safe disposition
★ Document quotes/findings; report suspected abuse to **Adult Protective Services**

rows.label: Don't
items: Do not confront the suspected abuser before arranging safety or disclose confidential plans unnecessarily
Do not require proof, a confession, or patient permission when reporting is legally mandatory
Poverty, accidental bruises, informed treatment refusal alone → insufficient evidence of neglect

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Immediate danger → emergency services; suspected crime may require police reporting
Capacitated adult can usually decline services; mandatory reporting may still apply under state law
Incapacity with unsafe care → protective intervention, surrogate review, possible emergency guardianship

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Inconsistent histories, different injury ages**, delayed care, controlling caregiver → investigate
Malnutrition, pressure injuries, medication deprivation → neglect; forced signatures → exploitation
Psychological abuse may leave no physical marks; arrange social work and confidential follow-up

elder-abuse-and-neglect.evidence: Not checked online; established ethics principles; reporting statutes vary by jurisdiction.

epididymitis.name: Epididymitis
epididymitis.scope: Acute epididymitis, sexually transmitted vs enteric pathogens by age, Prehn sign, empiric antibiotic regimens, ruling out torsion
epididymitis.core: Gradual unilateral posterior testicular pain with urinary or urethral inflammation suggests epididymitis; always assess for torsion first.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Sexually active younger adults: gonorrhea/chlamydia; older adults with obstruction/instrumentation: enteric organisms
Insertive anal intercourse permits both STI and enteric pathogens; exposure matters more than age

rows.label: Clues
items: Tender swollen epididymis, dysuria, fever, possible urethral discharge; cremasteric reflex often preserved
Prehn sign: elevation may relieve pain, but **cannot exclude torsion**
Sudden severe onset, nausea, high-riding/horizontal testis → surgical emergency

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Ascending urethral/urinary infection spreads through vas deferens → epididymal inflammation
Extension into testis causes epididymo-orchitis; edema can impair perfusion in severe disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ High torsion suspicion → **urgent urology/exploration**, without waiting for testing
Uncertain → **Doppler ultrasound**; epididymal hyperemia favors infection, absent testicular flow favors torsion
★ First-catch urine **gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT**, urinalysis, bacterial urine culture; HIV/syphilis testing
Negative ultrasound does not exclude epididymitis; persistent mass warrants alternative-diagnosis evaluation

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Empiric antibiotics after specimens; **scrotal support, NSAIDs**, relative rest
Treat before test results; regimen determined by likely pathogens, not age alone
Reevaluate if no improvement within **72 hours**; severe fever/pain or inability to adhere → hospitalization

rows.label: Complications
items: Abscess, testicular infarction, chronic scrotal pain, reduced fertility
Persistent swelling after treatment → assess tumor, TB, abscess, infarction

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ STI-associated infection: **partners from prior 60 days** need evaluation/presumptive treatment
Abstain until both partners treated and symptoms resolved; condoms reduce reinfection

rows.label: Mimics
items: Testicular torsion: abrupt pain, absent reflex; urgent detorsion required
Torsed appendage: focal upper-pole tenderness, blue-dot sign
Inguinal hernia: groin/scrotal mass, bowel symptoms, reducibility or strangulation

geriatric-assessment.name: Geriatric assessment
geriatric-assessment.scope: Comprehensive geriatric assessment, activities of daily living, instrumental ADLs, home safety, multidisciplinary care
geriatric-assessment.core: Comprehensive geriatric assessment integrates medical, functional, cognitive, psychological, and social findings into a coordinated plan aligned with the older adult’s goals.

rows.label: Definition
items: Identify reversible contributors to frailty, disability, drug harms, and unsafe living
Domains: gait, cognition, mood, nutrition, continence, senses, drugs, caregivers, home

rows.label: Interpret
items: ★ **IADL decline often precedes ADL decline**; establish baseline and change over time
Dependence identifies support needs; disability does not alone establish incapacity

rows.label: Use when
items: ★ New falls, functional loss, recurrent hospitalization, weight loss, polypharmacy, or caregiver strain
Ask patient goals; reconcile prescriptions, OTC drugs, supplements, adherence, and affordability
Assess home hazards, food access, transportation, social isolation, and suspected abuse

rows.label: Compare
items: ADLs: bathing, dressing, toileting, transferring, continence, feeding
IADLs: medications, finances, shopping, cooking, transport, housekeeping, communication
Screen cognition and depression; interpret performance in context of hearing, vision, education, language

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Acute cognitive change → delirium assessment**, not automatic dementia labeling
Chronologic age alone should not decide surgery, rehabilitation, or preventive care
★ Combine **PT/OT, nursing, pharmacy, social work**, and primary care into one prioritized plan

geriatric-assessment.evidence: Definitions and established geriatric practice; not checked online.

heart-failure.name: Heart failure
heart-failure.scope: HFrEF, HFpEF, acute decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic flash pulmonary edema, guideline-directed medical therapy, neurohormonal activation (RAAS, ADH-mediated hyponatremia)
heart-failure.core: Inadequate cardiac output or elevated filling pressures → pulmonary or systemic congestion, even with a normal ejection fraction.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: CAD, hypertension, valvular disease, cardiomyopathy, alcohol, cardiotoxic chemotherapy
Decompensation triggers: ischemia, infection, arrhythmia, missed diuretics, NSAIDs

rows.label: Clues
items: Orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, elevated JVP, crackles, dependent edema
S3 suggests volume overload; S4 suggests stiff ventricle
★ **Flash edema**: abrupt respiratory distress, severe hypertension, pink frothy sputum

rows.label: Pathophys
items: RAAS/sympathetic activation → vasoconstriction, sodium retention, adverse remodeling
Nonosmotic **ADH** release → dilutional hyponatremia; marker of advanced disease

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Echocardiography**: EF, valves, wall motion; ECG, CXR, BNP support diagnosis
Low BNP argues against HF; obesity lowers BNP, renal dysfunction raises it
Identify precipitant: troponin, CBC, electrolytes, creatinine; evaluate ischemic cause

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Acute congestion → **IV furosemide**; hypoxemia → oxygen; respiratory distress → noninvasive ventilation
★ Hypertensive pulmonary edema → **IV nitroglycerin**; shock → norepinephrine ± dobutamine, urgent cause correction
Start beta-blocker only when compensated; ACE inhibitor → ARNI requires 36-hour washout
MRA requires eGFR >30, K <5; persistent EF ≤35% despite GDMT → consider ICD

rows.label: Complications
items: Cardiorenal syndrome, ventricular arrhythmia, sudden death, hepatic congestion
Diuresis → hypokalemia; RAAS blockade → hyperkalemia, renal dysfunction; monitor creatinine/K

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Daily weights, sodium moderation, adherence; **continue GDMT after EF recovery**
Treat hypertension, CAD, AF; smoking cessation, exercise, influenza/pneumococcal vaccination

rows.label: Mimics
items: COPD: obstructive spirometry, hyperinflation
Nephrotic syndrome: heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia
PE: pleuritic pain, thrombotic risk, RV strain

heart-failure.evidence: Checked 2026-10-30: [ACC HFrEF 2024](https://www.acc.org/Latest-in-Cardiology/ten-points-to-remember/2024/03/06/19/22/2024-acc-expert-consensus-hfref); other points established teaching.

hyperthyroidism.name: Hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis
hyperthyroidism.scope: Graves disease, toxic multinodular goiter, toxic adenoma, subacute thyroiditis, thyroid storm, beta-blockers, thionamides, radioactive iodine
hyperthyroidism.core: Excess circulating thyroid hormone → heat intolerance, weight loss despite appetite, tremor, and tachycardia; hormone overproduction differs from destructive release.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Autoimmune history, female sex; older age favors autonomous nodules
Iodine load, amiodarone, exogenous thyroid hormone; infection/surgery can precipitate storm

rows.label: Clues
items: Hyperreflexia, frequent stools, proximal weakness, widened pulse pressure; older adults may have apathetic presentation
★ **Thyroid storm**: fever, delirium, severe tachyarrhythmia, vomiting, heart failure; clinical diagnosis

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Increased tissue metabolic activity and beta-adrenergic sensitivity explain systemic manifestations
Thionamides block thyroid peroxidase; PTU also reduces peripheral T4 → T3 conversion

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **TSH first → free T4**, total T3 if T4 normal; suppressed TSH with elevated hormones
TRAb establishes Graves; uncertain cause → radioactive iodine uptake, except pregnancy/lactation
Low uptake: thyroiditis/exogenous hormone; low thyroglobulin supports exogenous ingestion

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Symptom control: **propranolol**; caution in asthma or decompensated HF
★ Storm → ICU, cooling/fluids, beta-blockade if tolerated, **PTU → iodine ≥1 hour later**, hydrocortisone
Radioiodine contraindicated during pregnancy/lactation; significant active orbitopathy favors another definitive treatment
Compression/suspicious nodule → thyroidectomy after control; pregnancy: first-trimester PTU, later methimazole

rows.label: Complications
items: AF, embolism, osteoporosis, cardiomyopathy; radioiodine often → hypothyroidism
★ Thionamides: **fever/sore throat → stop drug, urgent CBC**; PTU → severe hepatotoxicity

rows.label: Prevention
items: Monitor free T4 early during treatment; TSH recovery lags
Smoking cessation for orbitopathy; definitive treatment before planned pregnancy when feasible

rows.label: Mimics
items: Panic disorder: episodic symptoms without thyroid biochemical abnormalities
Pheochromocytoma: paroxysmal headache, sweating, severe hypertension
Menopause: hot flashes with menstrual transition, normal thyroid testing

table.title: Etiology determines treatment
rows: Diffuse uptake; bruit, orbitopathy, pretibial myxedema
One hot nodule, suppressed surrounding tissue
NSAID; prednisone if severe; no thionamides

infective-endocarditis.name: Infective endocarditis
infective-endocarditis.scope: Native and prosthetic valve endocarditis, Duke criteria, prophylaxis, IV drug use endocarditis, blood culture diagnostic criteria
infective-endocarditis.core: Persistent bacteremia with valve infection causes systemic emboli, valve destruction, and immune-complex injury.

rows.label: Risk factors
items: Prosthetic valve, prior endocarditis, congenital valve abnormality, intracardiac device
Injection drug use → tricuspid involvement; healthcare exposure, indwelling vascular access

rows.label: Clues
items: Fever, new regurgitant murmur, embolic stroke, splenic infarct, hematuria
Janeway lesions painless; Osler nodes painful; splinter hemorrhages nonspecific
★ **New conduction block** → periannular abscess; right-sided disease → septic pulmonary emboli

rows.label: Pathophys
items: Endothelial injury → platelet-fibrin nidus → microbial adherence and vegetation
Immune complexes → glomerulonephritis; infected fragments disseminate through downstream circulation

rows.label: Dx
items: ★ **Three blood-culture sets before antibiotics**; separate peripheral draws unless resuscitation would be delayed
Major microbiology: **typical organism in ≥2 culture sets**, nontypical in ≥3; specialized serology/PCR also qualifies
★ **TTE → TEE** if prosthesis/high suspicion; major imaging: vegetation, abscess, perforation, new significant regurgitation
Definite clinical Duke: 2 major, 1 major + 3 minor, or 5 minor criteria
Minor: predisposition, fever, vascular phenomena, immunologic phenomena, nondiagnostic microbiology

rows.label: Tx
items: ★ Empiric **IV vancomycin + cefepime** for acutely ill/healthcare-associated cases; tailor to cultures and setting
MSSA → nafcillin/oxacillin or cefazolin; susceptible viridans streptococci → ceftriaxone
Prolonged pathogen-directed IV antibiotics; prosthetic infections need specialist regimen and early surgical evaluation
Surgery: heart failure, abscess, persistent bacteremia, fungal infection, or selected recurrent/large embolizing vegetations

rows.label: Complications
items: Acute regurgitation, heart failure, mycotic aneurysm, metastatic infection
Antibiotic nephrotoxicity, line infection; hemorrhage into embolic cerebral lesions

rows.label: Prevention
items: ★ Dental **amoxicillin** for prosthetic valve/material, previous IE, selected cyanotic/residual CHD, transplant valvulopathy
Good oral hygiene, sterile access; no routine prophylaxis for GI/GU procedures or isolated MVP

rows.label: Mimics
items: Nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis: cancer/autoimmune disease, sterile cultures
Atrial myxoma: positional obstruction, intracavitary mass; vasculitis: no infected vegetation

lifestyle-counseling.name: Lifestyle counseling
lifestyle-counseling.scope: Physical activity, healthy diet, weight loss, prediabetes prevention
lifestyle-counseling.core: Collaborative, specific behavior goals improve cardiovascular risk, functional health, weight, and progression from prediabetes to diabetes.

rows.label: Who
items: ★ Adults with **overweight/obesity, prediabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia**, or low activity
Assess food access, mobility, culture, sleep, stress, tobacco, alcohol, and readiness to change

rows.label: Schedule
items: ★ Aim **150 minutes/week moderate aerobic activity** plus strength training ≥2 days/week
Start below target if sedentary; progressive increases and reduced sitting still provide benefit
Children/adolescents: about 60 minutes daily activity; tailor to development and ability

rows.label: Special groups
items: Prediabetes: structured Diabetes Prevention Program; target 5–7% weight loss
Older adults: add balance/functional training; preserve protein intake and resistance exercise
Pregnancy: adapted activity and nutrition; avoid intentional weight-loss dieting

rows.label: Choice
items: ★ **Mediterranean/DASH pattern**: vegetables, fruit, legumes, whole grains, unsaturated fats
Reduce sugary drinks/refined foods; calorie deficit for weight loss; individualize macronutrients
Motivational interviewing, SMART goals, tracking, follow-up; intensive multicomponent obesity care

rows.label: Contraindications
items: Unstable angina, decompensated HF, acute illness → stabilize before vigorous exercise
Insulin/sulfonylureas → plan glucose monitoring and hypoglycemia prevention around activity

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ Metformin prevention for selected **high-risk prediabetes**; lifestyle support remains necessary
Weight-neutral benefits occur before major weight change; avoid judging success solely by scale
Relapse → revise barriers and goals, without blame

medical-errors-and-patient-safety.name: Medical errors and patient safety
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.scope: Near miss, adverse event, error disclosure, root cause analysis, structured sign-outs and handoffs
medical-errors-and-patient-safety.core: Protect the patient first, disclose errors honestly, and redesign systems to reduce recurrence.

rows.label: Principle
items: Just culture: distinguish human error, risky shortcuts, and reckless conduct
Psychological safety enables reporting; accountability and system improvement can coexist

rows.label: Do
items: ★ **Stabilize and mitigate harm**, notify supervising clinician, preserve relevant clinical information
★ Disclose facts, consequences, **apology**, treatment/prevention plans; update uncertainties
★ Report through institutional safety system; document clinical facts and disclosure in medical record

rows.label: Don't
items: Avoid concealment, altered records, premature blame, or speculation about causation
Do not rely on education alone when workflow permits predictable repeated errors

rows.label: Exceptions
items: Reckless impairment/dangerous conduct → remove from unsafe duties; institutional escalation

rows.label: Traps
items: ★ **Root cause analysis**: retrospective system investigation; identify multiple contributors
Failure mode and effects analysis: prospective hazard assessment before harm
Handoff: standardized I-PASS/SBAR, pending tasks, contingency plans, receiver synthesis/read-back
